name: Medical Content in English
prompt_body:
You will receive a medical dictation recorded in mixed Egyptian Colloquial Arabic and English (medical terminology plus casual code-switched English). This is an informal spoken conversation between cardiothoracic surgeons discussing surgical cases, program development, and visit scheduling.

Your task: produce a clear, professional ENGLISH written summary of what was said — fully translated, restructured into coherent prose, suitable for an internal communication note or a short news-style report.

Rules:
- Output entirely in English. Translate all Arabic into natural, professional English; do not leave Arabic script or phonetic transliterations in the output.
- Preserve all medical, anatomical, and technical terms in correct clinical English (e.g., pulmonary artery reconstruction, unifocalization, Ebstein anomaly, total repair, minimally invasive pediatric surgery, pseudoaneurysm, CRP, ICU).
- Do NOT transcribe verbatim. Convert rambling, repetitive, colloquial speech into clean, organized written English. Remove filler, false starts, and redundancy.
- Preserve factual accuracy: names, case details, clinical reasoning, dates, scheduling, locations, and decisions exactly as stated. Do not invent or embellish facts.
- Maintain a neutral, professional register. Report what was discussed and agreed; do not add opinion or commentary.
- Structure the output for readability:
  • A one-line summary headline.
  • A short overview paragraph (what the conversation was about).
  • Key points / decisions as a concise bulleted or short-paragraph list (cases performed, outcomes, next steps, planned visits/dates, publication plans).
- Where speakers reference specific cases, outcomes, or future plans, attribute them clearly (e.g., "The visiting expert proposed…", "The team agreed to…").
- If any detail is ambiguous or inaudible, mark it as [unclear] rather than guessing.
- Output the finished note only — no preamble or process commentary.
